chapters.title: Module 1 – Using language to express oneself on relationships within the family, school and the community

lessons.title: Situation 1: Interacting with mates, neighbours, adults and school authorities on community celebrations (modals)
Situation 2: Taking part in communal work (purpose, result, obligation; present and past perfect)
Situation 3: Settling community disputes (prepositions and prepositional phrases)
Situation 4: Taking part in recreational activities (conditionals 1, 2, 3)

chapters.title: Module 2 – Using language to express oneself in purchasing goods and services and on the principles of getting a job

lessons.title: Situation 1: Buying and selling articles and foodstuffs at a nearby store or market (polite requests and suggestions)
Situation 2: Requesting services (determiners and quantifiers)
Situation 3: Managing personal finances (adjectives as nouns; so do I, neither did he)
Situation 4: Developing and sharing interests in a trade, job or profession (partitive articles)

chapters.title: Module 3 – Using language to express oneself on safety measures and health risks

lessons.title: Situation 1: Visiting tourist sites (used to do, to be used to; gerunds)
Situation 2: Planting trees, gardening and protecting natural habitats (tag questions)
Situation 3: Preventing communicable diseases (passive and active voices)
Situation 4: Communicating with others on health issues (compound nouns and their plurals)

chapters.title: Module 4 – Using language to express oneself on promoting excellence, individual civic responsibility and basic freedoms

lessons.title: Situation 1: Developing a work culture and excellence at work (conjunctions)
Situation 2: Promoting individual civic responsibility (each other, one another; adverbs of negation)
Situation 3: Exercising democracy and tolerance
Situation 4: Promoting basic freedoms (phrasal verbs)

chapters.title: Module 5 – Using language to explore the modern media and information and communication technologies

lessons.title: Situation 1: Exploiting verbal and non-verbal information in modern media (used for, used with)
Situation 2: Using the new ICTs: web, MP3, USB drives, messaging apps ('how' questions)
Situation 3: Handling and maintaining machines and gadgets (expressing preferences; punctuation)
Situation 4: Maintaining netiquette (prepositions to talk about the internet)
